clue.text: Rich water source no longer fresh

parts.note: a well is a source of water drawn from underground
food that has gone off is no longer fresh

explanation.surface: A rich spring of water that has started to go stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-off has plenty of money, a common informal synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: Regulation upset eccentric French speaker

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a law is a regulation
a loon is a crazy or odd person

explanation.surface: An odd Francophone gets annoyed about the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Walloons are the French-speaking people of southern Belgium.

clue.text: Woodworking tool in hall at Hereford

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, spanning the word break

parts.note: letters running across the end of hall and the start of the next two words

explanation.surface: A carpentry machine housed in a hall in the cathedral city of Hereford.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins wood so it can be shaped with a cutting tool, a standard turner's machine.

clue.text: New mark of excellence in Glyndebourne speciality mostly alfresco

indicators.note: the first two items are placed inside the following word
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Glyndebourne is an English country house famous for its summer opera festival
N is the abbreviation for new
A1 means first-class, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: Glyndebourne's new top-rated show is largely staged outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Glyndebourne is an opera house in the Sussex countryside; A1 is the old Lloyd's Register top rating, written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco means in the fresh air, outdoors, which is what open-air means.

clue.text: Pay for article coming between extreme parts of chicken

indicators.note: something coming between two others sits in the gap separating them

parts.note: a bird's foot and its bill are at its two ends
the definite article

explanation.surface: Covering the cost of an item squeezed between a chicken's extremities.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot the bill is the idiom for paying the cost of something, often on someone else's behalf.

clue.text: Old painter showing origins of unique Celtic instrument

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only the opening letters of the next two words count

parts.note: the first letter of each of these two words
a bowed string instrument

explanation.surface: An old artist's work reveals the roots of some one-off Celtic musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Paolo Uccello was a fifteenth-century Florentine painter, famous for his experiments with perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: Uccello was an early Renaissance Italian artist, so he is an old painter by any measure.

clue.text: Deny rejecting official employment

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to refuse is to deny
a ref is a referee, a sports official

explanation.surface: Refusing to give an official a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Use as a noun means the employment of something for a purpose, as in the use of force.

clue.text: Painstaking group of travellers going round Spain

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a carful is as many people as fill a car
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A painstaking party of tourists touring Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful means taking great pains to avoid mistakes, so it is a near synonym of meticulous.

clue.text: Steward's assistant, never lead, unfortunately

indicators.note: something that turns out unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A deputy is told, sadly, that he will never be the one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A land-reeve was an official who assisted the steward of a large estate in managing the land.

clue.text: Overwhelm work on iron

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Being swamped by having to work on the ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to weigh heavily on someone, crushing them in spirit or by force.

clue.text: Nimble chap's put in illuminated sign, except for last letter

indicators.note: something put in another thing sits inside it, so one word is placed within another
the word for sign is taken with its final letter left off

parts.note: lit means lighted up
a chap is a he, and with the apostrophe s this reads as 'he's'
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: An agile man gets inserted into a glowing sign that is missing its final letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 'chap’s' is read as the contraction 'he is', and 'except for last letter' applies only to the sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithesome is a rarer form of lithe, meaning supple and moving easily, which is what nimble describes.

clue.text: Approach repair quickly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the period or path leading up to an event
second meaning: to sew or make something up hastily

explanation.surface: Advice to tackle a fix with speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the lead-in before an event or a jump, and to run up clothes is to stitch them fast.

clue.text: Last letter over backing a highly-regarded person

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the following words are read from right to left

parts.note: a gem is a person of great worth, so 'a gem'

explanation.surface: A final message has gone over to support someone respected.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled from one end; O is its scorebook abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final character of the Greek alphabet, so it is literally the last letter.

clue.text: Time to request church working group

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to ask for something is to request it
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: It is time to petition the church about some committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group of people brought together to work on one specific problem or job.

clue.text: Drunk is in Washington area, swallowing litres — a source of much pain

indicators.note: the word is placed inside the following abbreviation

parts.note: drunk in the sense of having drunk, sipped
L is the symbol for litres

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: Washington DC, the District of Columbia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk in Washington downing litres is a big headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' tempts as an anagram indicator, but it is the past participle of drink. DC, the District of Columbia, is the area containing Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipped disc is a spinal injury in which a cushion between vertebrae bulges out, notoriously painful.

clue.text: Enthusiast runs into part of golf course — obstacle beside the fairway?

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic, as in a fitness nut

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up inside it

parts.note: the tee is where each hole begins
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A keen golfer charges onto the tee, wary of hazards lining the fairway.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a tree is one obstacle a golfer might meet beside a fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees often line golf fairways and block wayward shots, and a nut tree is one such tree.

clue.text: Group overturned wobbly easel around large pieces of mosaic

indicators.note: overturned means flipped over, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: the jumbled word surrounds another letter
something wobbly is unsteady, so the letters shift out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Artists turn over a shaky easel surrounded by big chunks of mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first word is turned over; the wobbly letters then wrap round the abbreviation for large.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessellae are small tiles or cubes of stone or glass from which a mosaic is assembled.

clue.text: Not so much carrying log after one bout of poor health

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it within, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: less means a smaller amount
ln is the mathematical symbol for the natural logarithm

explanation.surface: Someone carrying less timber after one spell of feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Log here is the logarithm, written ln on a calculator, not a lump of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness is a period of sickness, which is exactly a spell or bout of poor health.

clue.text: Producer of stage works skinned zebra? Source of indignation

indicators.note: skinning removes the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a zebra is one kind of pedestrian street crossing in Britain, hence the question mark

indicators.note: the source of something is where it begins, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A cryptic hunt for an opera composer, a peeled zebra and some anger.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is a British road crossing marked with black and white stripes. Skinned, CROSSING becomes ROSSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini composed operas such as The Barber of Seville, works produced on the stage.

clue.text: Quickly list river fish originating in France

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
an eel is a fish
of can mean coming from, as in a man of Kent
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Rattling off the names of river fish native to France.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off is to recite a series of items rapidly and without effort.

clue.text: I take a long time to acquire right cameras?

indicators.note: acquiring something takes it in, so a letter is placed inside

parts.note: reads as 'I'm ages', I am taking ages
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are slow to pick up the correct photographic equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: IMAGES is 'I'm ages', informal for I am taking a long time; R goes before its final S. The question mark warns that cameras are only one kind of imager.
explanation.definitionFit: An imager is any device that records images, and a camera is the familiar example.

clue.text: Noblewoman, Early English, appearing in newspapers?

indicators.note: something appearing in a publication sits within it

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively
the initials of the two words

explanation.surface: A titled lady from medieval England turns up in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: EE goes inside PRESS. Early English is also the name of a Gothic architectural style, abbreviated EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress is a woman holding a peerage in her own right, or the wife of a peer: a noblewoman.

clue.text: Historic recording: company uplifted most of sound

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: uplifted means raised, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in sound in wind and limb

explanation.surface: A landmark album sees its label raise most of the audio quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like audio beside 'recording', but it means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal means momentous enough to mark a new era, which is what historic means in this sense.

clue.text: Poet readily suppressing source of folly

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down and keep it in

parts.note: soon can mean willingly, as in I would as soon go
an ass is a fool, so the source of foolishness

explanation.surface: A writer of verse eagerly keeping silly impulses in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of folly' wants to be its first letter, F; it is the fool who causes folly.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried Sassoon was an English poet best known for his First World War verse.

clue.text: Observed the writer, very blunt in speech

indicators.note: what is said in speech is heard rather than read, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: the writer of the clue is I, and a very blunt statement is bald

explanation.surface: An author describing being looked at by someone extremely frank in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is to look at it closely, an informal way of saying observed.

clue.text: Love in the current scenario is a refuge

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
as is means in the present state

explanation.surface: Finding a haven in love the way things stand now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it should put O inside the next words, but it only places love within the present situation.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile place in a desert, and figuratively any peaceful place of escape or shelter.

clue.text: Jabber, not mentioning your slight burn

indicators.note: leaving something unmentioned means dropping it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: something that jabs, a hypodermic needle
yr is the abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: Chattering on without mentioning your little burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jabber' looks like talking nonsense, but it is read as a thing that jabs.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to scorch lightly, burning just the surface or the ends.

clue.text: Uncovered foolish ideas in skateboard manoeuvre

indicators.note: removing a cover strips off the outside, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: follies are foolish acts or notions

explanation.surface: Exposed silly notions behind some skateboarding trick.
explanation.definitionFit: An ollie is a jump in skateboarding where the rider pops the board into the air without hands.

clue.text: Attack weak crew holding in first of oars

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for weak

indicators.note: a thing holding something keeps it inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A feeble rowing team pulls in on the first stroke and attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The crew is a rowing eight, which suits the oars; 'in' is not a link word here but letters to be held.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh into someone is to set about them vigorously, physically or in argument.

clue.text: Walk on water at the outset? Amazing!

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone stunned by a miracle of walking on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Wow is an exclamation of astonishment, used where someone might cry Amazing!

clue.text: French make no use of turning tool

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for French

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to waste something is to fail to use it

explanation.surface: French workers neglect to employ some revolving implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw for cutting curves in wood, a hand tool.

clue.text: Irish girl with reduced requirement for return after college

parts.note: Coll is an abbreviation for college

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so letters are read backwards
reducing cuts something short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a need is something required

explanation.surface: An Irish student cuts back her needs to go home after university.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleen comes from the Irish word cailín, meaning girl, and is used for a young Irishwoman.
